messages:
maria: Customer (AcmeMedia) opened a support ticket: intermittent missing trailing JSON object on SSE streams when they open many concurrent streams (~10-15). Started after SDK bump. Ticket: https://redwood.support/t/98712 :thinking_face:

samir: Can you paste the minimal logs / repro steps?

maria: Pasting trimmed server side log:
```
2026-03-15T18:22:03.123Z INFO stream-start conn=abcd1234 client=acme-01
2026-03-15T18:22:03.456Z INFO emit {"id":"m1","text":"hello"}
2026-03-15T18:22:03.789Z INFO emit {"id":"m2","text":"world"}
2026-03-15T18:22:03.901Z INFO conn-close conn=abcd1234 status=200
// client reports it only received m1
```

maria: Customer also supplied client snippets (python + node). Py snippet:
```python
# simplified
from sseclient import SSEClient
es = SSEClient(url, headers=headers)
for event in es:
    data = json.loads(event.data)
    process(data)
# multiple connections created in parallel from their runner
```

maria: Node snippet:
```js
const es = new EventSource(url);
es.onmessage = e => handle(JSON.parse(e.data));
// they spin up ~12 streams at once and tear down quickly when done
```

lee: Which SDK versions? Did they upgrade both py and ts clients?

maria: They were on python-sdk@0.19.2 and ts-sdk@1.3.0. They said it didn't happen on older pinned infra a few weeks ago.

samir: I ran a local stress repro: spin up 12 concurrent SSE clients, close them within 100-300ms after last event. I see ~5% of streams missing the last JSON object on the client side. Server logs show the emit but client didn't get final event.

julian: Thanks, looks like a regression introduced by the streaming transport refactor (pooled chunk buffers + faster backpressure path). My hypothesis: when connections tear down close-to-simultaneously we sometimes reclaim/reuse a buffer before the final chunk is flushed to the socket leading to the client missing the last event.

julian: Quick patch idea: on connection close ensure we call flushFinalChunk(conn) which pins the buffer until write completes. Also add a tiny safety drain (10ms) on pooled path for fast-close cases.

maria: Could that impact latency/cost? Customer cares about throughput but also correctness.

julian: Impact should be negligible at scale. This condition only triggers on very short-lived streams. We'll run perf tests.

dev-bot: Deployed canary: streaming/transport@v0.19.3-canary to staging (build link: https://ci.redwood/streaming/12345).

samir: Verified canary with the same stress harness — failure rate dropped to 0/500 runs.

maria: I pushed canary to customer staging and they confirmed it fixed the symptom. They asked for ETA on production rollout and whether there will be a patch release for 0.19.x clients.

julian: Plan: cut 0.19.3 with the flushFinalChunk fix and ship server runtime patch next prod deploy (ETA 48h). For client SDKs, we'll bump python-sdk to 0.19.3 with a safety guard too.

maria: Noted, forwarded ETA to customer. Leaving thread open until prod release. :thumbsup:
